_comment: Source of truth for what is published at https://vizora.cloud/tv and
`candidate` is the artifact verified by scripts/release/verify-display-apk.mjs.
`published` is the artifact currently live (null until the first publish); it is
the baseline the next release's signing certificate and versionCode are compared
`approval` encodes the two release gates. publish-display-apk.sh REFUSES to run
while either pair is null. Do not fill these in without the named human actually
confirming. Never put the keystore, its password, or any private key in this repo.
The canonical Vizora Android customer-signing identity.
Every publish — INCLUDING THE FIRST — must produce an APK whose signing
certificate equals canonicalCertSha256. The `published` baseline below only
protects release 2 onward; pinning here is what protects release 1, which is
exactly where the 2026-08-10 mismatch was found.
Pin this ONLY after the key passes full durability verification: private-key
entry exists, certificate SHA-256 known, keystore has a secure off-machine
backup, credentials recoverable by an authorized operator, and restoration
tested well enough to prove the key still signs. Record classification and
ownership only — never a password or private-key material.
_findings_2026_08_10: GATE B FAILED. The key that signed vizora-display-1.3.10-release.apk
(cert AA07524A…A5137982, created 2026-03-31) is NOT on the Windows build
machine. The only Android keystore there — vizora-tv android/vizora-release.jks,
single entry, alias vizora-display, created 2026-03-26 — carries a DIFFERENT
certificate: BE2320A5…3A9187A5. Not signed in CI, not the debug key, and no
other .jks/.keystore exists under the user profile or OneDrive.
DO NOT PUBLISH the existing 1.3.10 APK. Once canonicalCertSha256 is pinned to
a durable key, the verifier refuses that binary automatically — its cert will
_playStoreNote: Before customer rollout, compare the canonical sideload certificate with the
Google Play App Signing certificate. If they differ, pilot customers migrating
from the sideloaded APK to the Play Store build will need one uninstall +
reinstall (and will re-pair). Document it before the migration, not after.

approval._gateA: Artifact approval — confirm this exact APK is the intended client-pilot build, not merely the newest GitHub prerelease.
approval._gateB: Signing-key durability — confirm the release keystore has a secure off-machine backup and a recoverable password owned by an authorized operator. Record location CLASS and ownership only, never the key or password.
